newsitem.title: USA: Paine Webber stock rises on takeover rumors.
newsitem.headline: Paine Webber stock rises on takeover rumors.

text.p: The stock of PaineWebber Group Inc. rose sharply Friday on a published report that the brokerage was being considered as a potential takeover target by BankAmerica Corp. and others.

PaineWebber said later that contrary to the article in the Jan. 27 issue of Business Week, the firm's Chairman Donald Marron had not held conversations with the chairman of BankAmerica Corp. regarding a possible acquisition of Paine Webber by BankAmerica or a merger of the two firms.
An item in the Inside Wall Street column in Business Week said there had been talks between BankAmerica and PaineWebber about a combination.
PaineWebber stock rose $3.75 to $31.375 on the New York Stock Exchange, and BankAmerica rose $1 to $106.875.
Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Raphael Soifer said BankAmerica executives discussed the possiblity of buying a broker at a meeting with analysts on Thursday.

According to Soifer, chief financial officer Michael O'Neill said that, while BankAmerica likes the equity underwriting business and believes it would take too long to build a business internally, it also finds the asking prices of Wall Street firms too high.
O'Neill said BankAmerica would not overpay for an acquisiton, the analyst said.
"None of this would be consistent with buying PaineWebber which is primarily a retail brokerage rather than an equity underwriter," said Soifer.
